prompt: The search count stays constant, but a client update sends a suggestion request after every keystroke instead of waiting for a pause. What should capacity planning revisit?

options.text: Only stored query strings; client behaviour cannot change request load.
options.explanation: It changes how many intermediate prefixes generate requests.

options.text: Only the daily search count, which has not changed.
options.explanation: One search can now produce many more suggestion requests.

options.text: Nothing, because cancellation guarantees the server did no work.
options.explanation: Cancellation can arrive after work began and cannot be assumed to undo it.

options.text: Requests per search, cache reuse, peak arrival patterns and the latency budget.
options.explanation: Correct. Serving demand depends on the client contract as well as completed searches.

workedExample: Trace a typed query from keystrokes to network requests. Compare debounce behaviour, local reuse, cancellation and stale-response handling. Measure the resulting request stream before scaling the serving fleet.

link.title: Meta engineering: the life of a typeahead query

prompt: A measured immutable suggestion index and both versions needed during rollout fit in the chosen servers’ RAM. Load tests meet the latency target. What is a reasonable initial deployment?

options.text: Replicate the full index and add serving replicas as measured traffic requires, with failure headroom.
options.explanation: Correct. Any replica can answer any prefix, avoiding unnecessary routing and partial-shard failure paths.

options.text: Scan all matching queries in a relational store on every keystroke.
options.explanation: That abandons the supplied precomputed answers and requires a new performance justification.

options.text: Shard by the first English letter regardless of locale or observed traffic.
options.explanation: Letter distribution and alphabets differ; equal letter ranges do not imply balanced load.

options.text: Fetch individual index nodes from object storage for every lookup without measuring latency.
options.explanation: Snapshot publication and low-latency serving are different paths; this adds remote reads to each lookup.

workedExample: Check the complete memory footprint, including old and new versions and runtime overhead. If it fits and throughput is measured, replication keeps routing simple. Still test node and regional failures, warm-up and rollout bandwidth before assuming linear scaling.
